# 1 Kings Chapter 5 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** When King Hiram of Tyre heard that Solomon had been anointed king in his father's place, he sent envoys to him. Hiram had always been a close ally of David.

**2** Solomon sent back this message to Hiram:

**3** "You know that my father David could not build a temple for the name of the LORD his God because he was surrounded by wars on every side, until the LORD put all his enemies under his feet.

**4** But now the LORD my God has given me peace on every border. There is no enemy, no crisis.

**5** So I am planning to build a temple for the name of the LORD my God, just as the LORD told my father David: 'Your son, whom I will place on your throne after you — he is the one who will build the temple for my name.'

**6** Please order that cedars of Lebanon be cut for me. My workers will work alongside yours, and I will pay your workers whatever wages you set. As you know, we have no one who can match the Sidonians at cutting timber."

**7** When Hiram received Solomon's message, he was overjoyed. "Praise the LORD today," he said, "for giving David a wise son to rule this great nation!"

**8** Hiram sent his reply to Solomon: "I received your message. I will supply everything you need in cedar and cypress timber.

**9** My men will haul the logs from Lebanon down to the coast, where I'll have them lashed into rafts and floated by sea to wherever you specify. I'll have them broken apart there for you to collect. In return, you will supply food for my palace."

**10** So Hiram provided Solomon with all the cedar and cypress he wanted,

**11** and Solomon gave Hiram twenty thousand cors of wheat and twenty cors of pure olive oil annually for his household.

**12** The LORD gave Solomon wisdom, just as he had promised. There was peace between Hiram and Solomon, and they made a formal treaty.

**13** King Solomon conscripted laborers from all over Israel — thirty thousand men.

**14** He sent them to Lebanon in shifts of ten thousand per month: one month in Lebanon, two months at home. Adoniram was in charge of the labor force.

**15** Solomon also had seventy thousand common laborers and eighty thousand stonecutters working in the hills,

**16** plus thirty-three hundred foremen who supervised the workers.

**17** On the king's orders, they quarried large blocks of high-quality stone to lay a dressed-stone foundation for the temple.

**18** Solomon's builders, Hiram's builders, and craftsmen from Gebal shaped and prepared the timber and stone for the construction.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

1. **5:3-5 — the theological logic of timing**: Solomon explains why David couldn't build the temple: the kingdom wasn't at rest. Only peace makes sacred building possible. This isn't an excuse — it's a theology of worship that requires shalom as its precondition.

2. **5:7 — a pagan king praises YHWH**: Hiram of Tyre blesses Israel's God. Whether this reflects genuine reverence or diplomatic courtesy, it's remarkable. Solomon's reign attracts international acknowledgment of YHWH.

3. **5:13-16 — the cost of glory**: The temple workforce numbers over 180,000 people. This is an extraordinary mobilization of human labor. The text reports it neutrally, but the reader should hear an echo of Egypt: Israel was once the conscripted labor force. Now Israel conscripts its own.

4. **5:12 — "they made a formal treaty"**: Solomon and Hiram's relationship is covenantal, not merely commercial. This international partnership foreshadows the temple's universal vision — a house of prayer for all nations built by international cooperation.

5. **5:17 — "high-quality stone"**: The Hebrew ʾavnei yaqar means precious, costly stones. The foundation itself is made of premium materials. The theology: what is offered to God starts with the best, from the ground up.

— PNEUMA
